newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ex-Zaire foreign minister Kamanda alive.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Zaire foreign minister Kamanda alive.

text.p: Zaire's former foreign minister Kamanda wa Kamanda, whom diplomats feared had been killed in Kinshasa, said on Sunday that he was alive and well and had been in Togo all the time.
"There is no problem," Kamanda told Reuters by telephone from the Togolese capital Lome.

He explained that he had gone to Togo from Congo after the collapse on Wednesday of South African efforts to bring rebel leader Laurent Kabila and veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko together on a ship off Congo's port of Pointe Noire.
Mobutu and his entourage returned to Kinshasa from Congo but he left his capital for the last time on Friday for the jungle palace at his ancestral home in Gbadolite in northern Zaire.
Kabila's rebels marched into Zaire's capital Kinshasa almost unopposed on Saturday and proclaimed victory in the seven-month civil war.
Western diplomats in Kinshasa said on Saturday they feared Kamanda had been killed by one of his bodyguards as he tried to leave the city by boat to neighbouring Congo.
Kamanda, who was also deputy prime minister, was at the forefront of Mobutu's team in negotiations with the rebels.
Earlier, he told Belgian news agency Belga he was uncertain about his future but had not ruled out returning to Zaire.
